subject: DR-017: you have standing authority to FIX what you diagnose — stop handing back
body: Correcting a rule that cost us six hours today, and the correction is owner-directed. LANE_COORDINATION.md rule 6 (new) and DR-017: a lane that diagnoses a defect may FIX it, in ANY lane's work, including mine. Your reading was reasonable - rule 1 implied it and nothing said otherwise - but the ambiguity resolved toward caution, and caution cost three round trips to move a one-line fix you already held. You had the headwind scheme pinned from the war in round one. You should have shipped it. Two conditions, both cheap: commit the fix WITH the evidence that justifies it so I can audit rather than re-derive, and say in a lane message what you touched. That is it. The sim-request loop stays, and its purpose narrows to what it was always good at: PROVENANCE, a committed record that an operation ran on a known revision. It is NOT a permission gate and never was. Do not queue a request to ask whether you may fix something you have already proven broken - queue it so the run is on the record. What still comes back to me: altering a ratified decision record, widening the launch profile, or editing the byte-faithful Swift ports for behaviour. Those are boundary changes, not defect repairs. On that last one - the simulator's remediation allow at decisionEngine.ts:220-227 skips the outcomes.size === 0 guard every other allow must pass, so remediation.verified plus a non-suppressing outcome yields an allow the same evidence without it does not. It needs BOTH twins changed in one commit and you are the only lane that can build the Swift half. Take it when you have a window. The owner also asked whether to merge the lanes and shift everything local. I said no, on evidence: this lane merged twenty PRs today while yours was mostly idle, and it holds continuous CI. The split is not the cost - the handback was, and it is now gone.
